answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable resource—such as a refundable stake—before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. The protocol caps each account’s influence and slashes the stake when independently verified fraud is proven, so spawning a thousand accounts requires a thousand funded deposits, not just fresh keys. A zephyr of cheap registrations cannot swamp an orchard of trusted agents; the attacker pays a real capital cost and risks losing it, while honest agents recover their stake. The delta is that identity creation stops being free.
